title: Geometry - Lesson 8 Practice: Composite Perimeter
description: Practice tracing the outside boundary and adding side lengths to find perimeter.

questions.question: When finding the perimeter of a composite figure, which sides should be added?
questions.explanation: Perimeter is the distance around the outside boundary. Interior dividing lines are not part of the perimeter.

questions.question: An L-shaped figure has outside side lengths 10 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm, 3 cm, 4 cm, and 7 cm. What is the perimeter? Enter just the number.
Perimeter answers use square units because perimeter is measured around a shape.
questions.explanation: Perimeter is a length around the shape, so it uses linear units such as cm, m, or units.

questions.question: A rectilinear figure has a total width of 15 m. The top is split into 9 m and a missing horizontal side. What is the missing horizontal side? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: The horizontal parts across the top must match the total width: 15 - 9 = 6 m.

questions.question: A student adds a dashed interior line when finding perimeter. What is the likely mistake?
options: Counting a side that is not on the outside boundary
questions.explanation: Interior lines may help split a shape, but they are not part of the outside distance around the figure.

questions.question: Find the perimeter if the outside boundary sides are 8 cm, 5 cm, 3 cm, 2 cm, 5 cm, and 7 cm. Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: Add the outside boundary lengths: 8 + 5 + 3 + 2 + 5 + 7 = 30 cm.

questions.question: Explain how tracing the boundary helps you find the perimeter of a composite figure.
questions.correctAnswer: Tracing the boundary helps me follow the outside of the figure one side at a time, so I add each outside side once and do not count interior lines.
questions.explanation: A complete answer should mention following the outside boundary and avoiding interior sides.

questions.question: A shape has total height 12 cm. One vertical part is 5 cm and another vertical part is missing. How can you find the missing vertical length?
questions.correctAnswer: Subtract the known vertical part from the total height: 12 - 5 = 7 cm.
questions.explanation: For rectilinear figures, vertical lengths that go down must balance the total vertical distance, so subtraction finds the missing part.
